note: Not ready to start coding. Several blocking doc gaps are still open with no owner answer (storage retention cap left as open RFC, WAL/GP8 doc-gap item marked 'test' with no real content pending staff re-answer, ctx_upgrade headless-consent mechanism not accepted yet). Questions below are new, not repeats.

questions.question: ADR-0001 line 8 says v1 adapters used 'runtime fallbacks' that hid bugs, and the owner decision bans fallback chains in v2. Does this ban also cover ctx_upgrade and ctx_doctor internal retry/backoff logic (e.g. the withRetry ladder at src/db-base.ts:432, delays [100,500,2000]), or is that retry ladder explicitly exempt since it is not a 'fallback chain' but a busy-timeout retry? TECH-SPEC does not say which bucket the retry ladder falls into.
questions.why: If the no-fallback-chain rule applies to the retry ladder, GP8's answer (confirmed last round as the retry ladder) would itself be banned by ADR-0008/ADR-0001, contradicting the GP8 target in TECH-SPEC line 296. Needs a one-line owner clarification before M0 storage code can reuse the v1 retry ladder.

questions.question: The owner rule says v1 unit tests stay until v2 passes the kept ones, and v2 only needs to keep 'at least the solid parts.' Which file or doc lists the specific tests considered 'solid' vs ones expected to be dropped? tests/store-bytecap.test.ts and the SSRF guard tests (for ef9eeaa4/8ef04c6a) look safety-critical and should be on the keep list — is that confirmed?
questions.why: Without a named keep-list, M0 cannot know which failing v1 tests block a release vs which are expected casualties of the rewrite, and the SSRF regression (#476) could silently re-break if its test is dropped.

questions.question: ADR-0013's weekly drift check for branch protection settings on main has no automation owner named (cron, GitHub Action, or manual). Given the owner's CronCreate/schedule tooling exists in this workspace, should the weekly check be a scheduled cloud routine, or a GitHub Action in the repo? TECH-SPEC does not say where this check runs.
questions.why: This decides whether M0 needs to ship a workflow file or a schedule/cron artifact; currently nothing in the repo implements the 'weekly check' ADR-0013 promises.

git_archaeology.finding: Confirms prior round's answer: MAX_CHUNK_BYTES is a per-chunk cap only, introduced for plain-text chunking, never extended to a total-index cap. No separate commit touches total DB size. Supports keeping storage Q7b as an open RFC rather than reusing 4096 for a different purpose.
